label: A/B testing
plain_descriptions: splitting users between two variants of a screen or feature to see which one performs better
controlled trial where real users are randomly split to measure which design drives higher conversions
summary: A randomized experimental method where two variants of a digital experience are shown to visitors simultaneously to determine which drives superior outcomes.

label: Acceptance criteria
plain_descriptions: specific checklist of conditions that a user story must satisfy before being marked complete
unambiguous rules showing developers and testers exactly how a feature should behave
summary: A predefined set of conditions, behaviors, and boundary checks that a specific user story must satisfy to be accepted.

label: Agent
plain_descriptions: an AI system that plans steps and uses tools to achieve goals independently
a software assistant that observes its environment, takes actions, and completes tasks
summary: An autonomous AI system that reasons over objectives, breaks goals into sequential steps, and interacts with tools and environments to complete tasks.

label: Benchmark
plain_descriptions: standardized test suites used to measure AI model accuracy and hardware speed
common evaluation exams allowing different AI systems to be fairly compared
summary: A standardized test suite and measurement protocol used to evaluate and compare the accuracy, throughput, latency, or energy efficiency of models and hardware.

label: Application Programming Interface (API)
plain_descriptions: a defined bridge that allows two software systems to talk to each other
a digital waiter taking requests from one application to another
summary: A set of defined rules, protocols, and endpoints enabling different software applications to communicate and exchange data.

label: Endpoint
plain_descriptions: the specific web address where an app sends requests to get certain information
a digital front door where external software asks a server to do something
summary: A dedicated network address and URL path exposed by an API where clients access a specific service or resource.

label: Attention mechanism
plain_descriptions: an AI technique that weighs which input words matter most at each step
the computational method letting models focus dynamically on relevant context
summary: A mathematical algorithm allowing neural models to calculate dynamic relevance weights between all tokens within an input sequence.

label: Autoscaling
plain_descriptions: automatically adding more servers when traffic spikes and removing them when things quiet down to save money
the system capability that expands or shrinks computing power based on real-time demand
summary: A cloud mechanism that automatically adjusts the number of active computing resources up or down based on real-time demand metrics.

label: Batch size
plain_descriptions: the number of training examples processed together in one forward and backward step
how many data samples an AI looks at before updating its internal weights
summary: The number of training samples processed simultaneously in a single iteration before the model parameters are updated.

label: Blue-green deployment
plain_descriptions: running two identical environments side by side and switching user traffic instantly to the new one
a release technique that eliminates downtime by preparing updates in a cloned backup environment
summary: A deployment strategy that provisions two identical production environments (Blue and Green), shifting all traffic from the active to the idle environment upon validation.

label: Breaking change
plain_descriptions: a modification in software or an API that breaks existing programs depending on it
an update that requires downstream developers to rewrite parts of their code to keep working
summary: A modification in a software interface, dependency, or system component that breaks backward compatibility and necessitates code adjustments in dependent systems.

label: Burndown chart
plain_descriptions: visual graph showing remaining work decreasing day by day throughout a sprint
progress tracking chart comparing actual remaining effort against an ideal completion slope
summary: A graphical representation of work left to do versus time, utilized by agile squads to forecast sprint completion trajectories.

label: Cache
plain_descriptions: a fast temporary storage area saving frequent answers so the computer skips slow re-calculations
keeping copies of popular web pages in memory so users don't wait for slow database queries
summary: A high-speed data storage layer that stores a subset of transient data so future requests are served faster than accessing primary storage.

label: Canary release
plain_descriptions: testing a new software version on a tiny percentage of real users before releasing it to everyone
a gradual rollout technique that exposes early bugs safely without risking the entire user base
summary: A deployment technique that exposes a new software release to a small fraction of production traffic to validate behavior before broader rollout.

label: Content Delivery Network (CDN)
plain_descriptions: a worldwide network of caching servers that delivers web pages and images quickly from locations near the user
a distributed cache that speeds up websites by serving files from nearby edge servers
summary: A geographically distributed network of proxy servers that caches and delivers web content to users with low latency and high availability.

label: Chain-of-thought prompting
plain_descriptions: asking the AI to think step by step
making the AI show its working before the answer
summary: A prompting technique that asks a model to reason through intermediate steps before it gives the final answer.

label: Churn rate
plain_descriptions: percentage of customers who stop using or paying for a service during a given time period
rate at which subscribers cancel memberships or abandon an application
summary: The share of paying users who stop, by cancelling or not renewing, during a given period.

label: CI/CD
plain_descriptions: automatically building, testing, and shipping code changes whenever engineers push work
the automated pipeline that moves software from development to live production servers
summary: A modern engineering methodology uniting frequent source integration with automated regression testing and reliable application deployment.

label: Pipeline
plain_descriptions: the step-by-step automated workflow that builds, tests, and packages code changes
the scripted sequence that takes software from a commit to a deployable artifact
summary: A defined sequential series of automated execution steps that compiles, tests, and packages application updates.

label: Code review
plain_descriptions: having teammate developers examine your code changes before merging
a peer inspection of source code to catch bugs and uphold standards
summary: A collaborative peer-review practice where software engineers systematically examine proposed code changes to identify defects, enforce architectural standards, and share knowledge.

label: Compound Interest
plain_descriptions: interest on interest
money snowballing because earnings get added back to the pile
summary: Interest calculated on both the initial principal and the accumulated interest from previous periods.

label: Image
plain_descriptions: the static template or blueprint used to create and run containers
a frozen snapshot of software files, system libraries, and startup commands
summary: An immutable, read-only package containing application binaries, libraries, configuration files, and metadata required to launch a container.

label: Context engineering
plain_descriptions: the practice of carefully designing and managing everything fed into an AI's context window
organizing tokens, instructions, tools, and history to maximize AI accuracy and reduce cost
summary: The disciplined practice of curating, structuring, compressing, and caching the information loaded into a model's context window to optimize performance and efficiency.

label: Context window
plain_descriptions: how much text the AI can keep in mind at once
the AI’s working memory limit
summary: The maximum amount of text, counted in tokens, that a model considers in one request, covering the prompt, the conversation so far and its reply.

label: Cookie
plain_descriptions: small browser file websites save to remember your login
web tracker banner you click accept on
summary: A small piece of data stored on the user's browser by websites to retain state and track browsing activity.

label: Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS)
plain_descriptions: a browser security check deciding if one website can fetch data from another domain
the rules preventing malicious websites from secretly querying your banking API
summary: A browser security protocol using special HTTP headers that lets an API grant specific foreign websites permission to fetch its content.

label: Cross-site request forgery (CSRF)
plain_descriptions: an attack that tricks your browser into making unwanted money transfers on sites where you are logged in
clicking a trap link on an external page that secretly submits a form to change your account email
summary: An attack that tricks an authenticated web browser into sending unauthorized commands to a vulnerable web application without the user’s consent.

label: Customer lifetime value (CLV)
plain_descriptions: total amount of money a business expects to earn from a customer throughout their entire relationship
projected net profit or revenue generated by a single user account over its lifespan
summary: The projected total revenue or profit that a business anticipates earning from a single customer throughout the duration of their relationship.

label: Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)
plain_descriptions: the standardized global dictionary of publicly recognized cybersecurity flaws and software bugs
an official tracking code like CVE-2021-44228 identifying a specific security flaw
summary: A publicly available list of standardized identifiers for cybersecurity vulnerabilities and exposures.

label: Daily active users (DAU)
plain_descriptions: count of unique people who open and interact with an application in a single day
vital metric tracking daily user volume and ongoing product engagement
summary: The total count of unique individuals who initiate a meaningful interaction with a software application within a 24-hour day.

label: Daily Scrum
plain_descriptions: quick fifteen-minute daily morning meeting for developers to sync on sprint progress
brief stand-up check-in where teammates share achievements, plans, and immediate blockers
summary: A 15-minute daily inspect-and-adapt event for developers to synchronize activities and plan the next 24 hours of work.

label: Data lake
plain_descriptions: a huge digital reservoir where companies store raw data in any format until needed
a flexible storage pool holding audio, text, images, and logs without forcing strict table structures
summary: A scalable storage repository designed to retain massive volumes of raw multi-format information without requiring an upfront database schema.

label: Data pipeline
plain_descriptions: an automated series of steps moving information from where it is created to where it is used
software plumbing that pumps live data from user clicks into analytics systems
summary: An automated sequence of processes that ingests, processes, and transfers raw data from source systems to destination storage.

label: Data warehouse
plain_descriptions: a central database designed specifically for business analysis and fast executive reporting
a giant organized filing room where companies store cleaned historical business records
summary: A centralized, relational repository that aggregates structured historical data from across an organization to power business intelligence and reporting.

label: Index
plain_descriptions: a sorted lookup helper that lets the database find specific rows in milliseconds instead of scanning the whole disk
an alphabetical index at the back of a book pointing directly to table rows
summary: A specialized data structure associated with a database table that accelerates record retrieval at the expense of extra storage and slower writes.

label: Migration
plain_descriptions: a version-controlled script that safely updates database table layouts as software evolves
a step-by-step code file for adding new columns or tables to live databases
summary: A version-controlled set of programmatic scripts that safely alter database schemas over time without losing existing data.

label: Replication
plain_descriptions: copying database records automatically to backup servers so the system survives hardware failures
syncing data across multiple database copies so heavy user reads don't slow down writes
summary: The continuous electronic copying of data from one database server to one or more replica servers to ensure high availability and read scalability.

label: Schema
plain_descriptions: the overall architectural blueprint defining the tables, columns, and rules in a database
the formal structural layout describing what kinds of data a database is allowed to hold
summary: The formal structural blueprint of a database that defines tables, fields, data types, relationships, and integrity constraints.

label: Transaction
plain_descriptions: an all-or-nothing group of database operations that either completely succeeds or leaves data untouched
a safe execution wrapper ensuring money transfers debit one account and credit another atomically
summary: A sequence of database operations executed as a single, atomic unit of work satisfying ACID properties.

label: Dataset
plain_descriptions: a structured collection of examples used to teach or test AI
the organized data gathered together for machine learning experiments
summary: A structured collection of data records, features, and targets partitioned to train, validate, and benchmark algorithms.

label: Deep learning
plain_descriptions: machine learning powered by deep neural networks with many hidden layers
advanced AI techniques that automatically learn rich representations from raw data
summary: A specialized subset of machine learning utilizing multi-layered neural networks to extract hierarchical feature representations directly from complex data.

label: Definition of Done (DoD)
plain_descriptions: shared quality checklist that every piece of work must meet before being considered finished
formal agreement covering code reviews, automated tests, documentation, and deployment steps
summary: A formal commitment detailing the technical and quality standards that every product increment must satisfy to be release-ready.

label: Deprecation
plain_descriptions: officially warning developers that a feature will be removed in a future update
marking old code as discouraged from use while keeping it working for now
summary: The practice of marking a software feature, API, or package as obsolete and discouraged from use, signaling that it will be removed in a future release.

label: Design pattern
plain_descriptions: a reusable template or battle-tested solution to a commonly occurring coding problem
a proven blueprint for structuring software components to solve standard architectural challenges
summary: A named, proven way of structuring code that solves a design problem developers meet again and again, such as creating objects or reacting to changes.

label: Distributed tracing
plain_descriptions: following a single user request as it travels across dozens of microservices to pinpoint where delays occur
a map showing the exact path and timing of an operation through connected servers
summary: A monitoring method that tracks the lifecycle of an execution request as it travels across multiple networked services and processes.

label: Domain Name System (DNS)
plain_descriptions: the internet phonebook that translates human-friendly website names like example.com into computer IP addresses
the directory service connecting domain names to web server numbers
summary: The hierarchical, decentralized naming system that translates human-readable domain names into numerical IP addresses for network routing.

label: Docker
plain_descriptions: the most popular software tool for building, running, and managing containers
the platform that popularised container packaging for modern software development
summary: An open commercial platform providing tooling to build, share, package, and execute application containers using host operating system virtualization.

label: Edge case
plain_descriptions: an unusual or extreme scenario that occurs only at the outer limits of operating parameters
a rare condition or extreme input that software must handle without failing
summary: A problem or operational situation that occurs only at extreme minimum or maximum operating parameters, testing the boundaries of system resilience.

label: Embedding
plain_descriptions: turning words into a list of numbers so a computer can compare meanings
numbers that place similar ideas close together
summary: A list of numbers learned by a model to represent an item such as a word or a document, so that similar items end up close together.

label: Encryption
plain_descriptions: scrambling secret information into unreadable code that only someone with the correct key can unlock
locking confidential data with a digital key so eavesdroppers see only scrambled nonsense
summary: The cryptographic process of encoding plaintext into ciphertext so that only authorized parties with the matching decryption key can read it.

label: End-to-end test
plain_descriptions: simulating a complete real user journey through the entire application from start to finish
testing an entire system including frontend, backend, database, and third-party integrations together
summary: A comprehensive testing methodology that validates the flow of an application from the user interface down through all underlying backend services and databases.

label: Environment variable
plain_descriptions: a dynamic key-value setting stored outside software code to configure how it behaves in different environments
a configuration variable provided by the operating system to running programs
summary: A dynamic key-value pair stored in the operating system environment that configures program behavior without altering application source code.

label: Epic
plain_descriptions: large body of work that spans multiple sprints and is split into several user stories
major product initiative or feature theme organized across a longer development timeframe
summary: A substantial strategic initiative in agile software delivery that encompasses a collection of related user stories delivered over several sprints.

label: Epoch
plain_descriptions: one complete pass of an entire training dataset through an AI model
a full cycle of training where every single example has been seen once
summary: One complete training cycle during which the learning algorithm processes every sample in the training dataset exactly once.

label: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL)
plain_descriptions: pulling data from various places, cleaning it up, and saving it into a central analytics database
the three-step data pipeline that prepares raw business numbers for dashboards and reports
summary: A data integration process that extracts data from multiple sources, transforms it to meet analytical requirements, and loads it into a destination store.

label: Feature flag
plain_descriptions: a software switch that turns a feature on or off without deploying new code
a configuration toggle allowing gradual rollout of features to specific users
summary: A software engineering technique that enables or disables functionality remotely at runtime through configuration without altering and redeploying source code.

label: Few-shot prompting
plain_descriptions: showing the AI a few examples before asking
teaching by examples inside the question
summary: A prompting technique that includes a few worked examples of the task so the model follows the same pattern.

label: Fine-tuning
plain_descriptions: training an existing AI a bit more on your own examples
teaching a ready-made model a specialised job
summary: Further training of a pre-trained model on a smaller task-specific dataset so it performs better on that task or style.

label: Function calling
plain_descriptions: letting the AI press buttons in other apps
the AI asking your code to fetch data or run an action
summary: A model capability to reply with a structured request to call a tool the developer defined; the app runs it and returns the result.

label: Branch
plain_descriptions: an independent line of work in a repository allowing safe experimentation
a movable pointer pointing to the latest commit in an isolated development path
summary: A lightweight movable reference pointing to a specific commit within a Git repository that represents an independent timeline of development.

label: Commit
plain_descriptions: a saved snapshot recording the exact state of project files with an explanatory note
a permanent record in the repository history describing what was changed and who changed it
summary: An immutable snapshot of staged changes recorded into Git repository history, associated with author metadata, timestamp, parent hashes, and a descriptive log message.

label: Rebase
plain_descriptions: moving your branch commits so they sit on top of the newest commit of another branch
rewriting Git history to produce a neat, linear sequence of project changes
summary: A Git command that moves or reapplies a sequence of commits from one branch on top of a new base tip, creating a linear history.

label: Graphics Processing Unit (GPU)
plain_descriptions: high-performance computer chips designed to handle massive parallel math for AI
the dedicated hardware processors that accelerate neural network training and inference
summary: A specialized electronic processor optimized for high-throughput parallel execution of mathematical matrix operations essential for deep learning.

label: Gradient descent
plain_descriptions: the core optimization math that guides AI models toward lower error
taking small steps down a mathematical slope to find the best model weights
summary: An iterative optimization algorithm that updates model parameters in the opposite direction of the loss function gradient to minimize prediction error.

label: GraphQL
plain_descriptions: an API tool that lets client apps request only the exact data fields they need
a single query language for frontends to fetch custom data shapes in one go
summary: An open query language and runtime for APIs that allows clients to request exact data shapes and consolidate multiple resources in one request.

label: Grounding
plain_descriptions: anchoring an AI's answers in verified factual documents to prevent made-up facts
ensuring a model's statements are directly tied to real, verifiable source citations
summary: The process of constraining a model's outputs to factual, verifiable evidence retrieved from trusted external data sources.

label: Guardrail
plain_descriptions: safety filters around a chatbot
rules that block harmful or off-topic AI answers
summary: A control around a model’s inputs or outputs that detects and blocks unsafe, off-policy or off-topic content.

label: Hallucination
plain_descriptions: when the AI confidently makes things up
a made-up fact or fake citation from a chatbot
summary: Output from a generative model that sounds plausible but is false or unsupported, presented as if it were fact.

label: Hashing
plain_descriptions: turning any piece of text into a unique fixed-length fingerprint that cannot be reversed
a one-way mathematical transformation commonly used to store passwords safely
summary: A cryptographic process that transforms arbitrary input data into a fixed-length string of characters using an irreversible one-way mathematical algorithm.

label: Hotfix
plain_descriptions: an emergency patch deployed straight to production to repair a critical defect
a fast, targeted fix addressing an urgent live outage outside the normal release cycle
summary: An expedited software patch created and deployed directly to production systems outside standard release cycles to resolve critical defects or security flaws.

label: HTTP status code
plain_descriptions: three-digit numbers that explain whether a web request succeeded or what went wrong
the server’s quick status signal like 404 not found or 200 ok
summary: A standardized three-digit integer returned by a server indicating the outcome of a client’s HTTP request.

label: Hyperparameter
plain_descriptions: configuration settings chosen by engineers before starting AI training
the external dials and knobs controlling how an algorithm learns
summary: An external configuration setting specified prior to training that governs how the model architecture is structured and optimized.

label: Idempotency
plain_descriptions: the property where executing an action multiple times produces the exact same result as doing it once
safely retrying an operation without causing duplicate charges or unintended side effects
summary: A property of an operation whereby performing it multiple times with the same parameters produces the identical outcome and system state as performing it a single time.

label: Image classification
plain_descriptions: an AI vision task that assigns a single overall label to an entire picture
identifying what main object or category is shown in a photo
summary: A computer vision task in which an algorithm analyzes an entire image and assigns it one or more discrete categorical labels from a predefined taxonomy.

label: Incident
plain_descriptions: an unplanned event that breaks software or degrades service quality for users
a sudden technical emergency that requires immediate engineering intervention
summary: An unplanned interruption, degradation, or disruption of an IT service that impairs business operations or user experience.

label: Inference
plain_descriptions: running a trained AI model to get live answers or classifications
using an existing model on new inputs without changing its weights
summary: The operational stage where a trained model processes live inputs to generate predictions, decisions, or outputs without updating its parameters.

label: Infrastructure as code (IaC)
plain_descriptions: setting up servers, databases, and networks using code files rather than clicking around in cloud consoles
managing computer infrastructure through version-controlled text files that can be reviewed and tested
summary: The practice of managing, provisioning, and configuring IT infrastructure through machine-readable definition files rather than manual procedures.

label: Integration test
plain_descriptions: checking whether different software parts work properly when joined together
testing real interactions between code, databases, and connected services
summary: An automated test that verifies whether multiple software components, modules, or external systems cooperate and exchange data correctly.

label: Interest Rate
plain_descriptions: percentage fee charged for borrowing money
percentage reward earned on savings per year
summary: The proportion of an amount loaned which a lender charges as interest to the borrower, typically expressed as an annual percentage.

label: Jailbreak
plain_descriptions: tricking a chatbot into breaking its own safety rules
prompts that make the AI say what it should refuse
summary: A prompt designed to make a model ignore its safety guidelines and produce content it is meant to refuse.

label: JSON
plain_descriptions: a universal text format used to send data between websites and servers
human-readable curly-brace text organizing names and values in software
summary: A lightweight, text-based data interchange format built on key-value pairs and ordered lists that is easy for humans to read and machines to parse.

label: JSON Web Token (JWT)
plain_descriptions: a compact digitally signed text token used to prove your identity across web requests
a three-part encrypted-looking string that carries user login claims inside an http header
summary: A self-contained web token format conveying verifiable identity assertions through encoded header, payload, and digital signature segments.

label: Kanban
plain_descriptions: visual project management board that tracks work across columns and limits tasks in progress
continuous delivery system focused on smoothing workflow and eliminating production bottlenecks
summary: A visual workflow management method designed to optimize continuous flow, limit work in progress, and maximize efficiency.

label: Distillation
plain_descriptions: training a smaller, faster AI model to mimic the knowledge of a huge model
transferring wisdom from an expert AI teacher into a compact student model
summary: A model compression technique where a compact student model is trained on output probability distributions generated by a larger, pre-trained teacher model.

label: Key Performance Indicator (KPI)
plain_descriptions: measurable target tracking whether a company or team is meeting its core operational goals
key business metric showing the ongoing performance and financial health of a product
summary: A quantifiable metric tracking ongoing operational efficacy and business performance against strategic benchmarks.

label: Kubernetes
plain_descriptions: an orchestration platform that automatically deploys, scales, and heals containers across clusters of machines
the industry standard control system for managing container fleets in production
summary: An open-source container orchestration system for automating deployment, scaling, management, and self-healing of containerized applications.

label: Pod
plain_descriptions: the smallest deployable unit in Kubernetes, containing one or more tightly linked containers
a shared wrapper that gives grouped containers the same IP address and storage volumes
summary: The smallest deployable computing unit in Kubernetes, encapsulating one or more tightly coupled containers sharing network and storage resources.

label: Latency
plain_descriptions: the time delay between sending a request and receiving the answer back over a network
how long you wait for a website or server to respond after clicking
summary: The time delay incurred for data to travel across a network from its source to its destination and return.

label: Principle of least privilege
plain_descriptions: giving users and apps only the exact minimum permissions required to perform their daily job
the security rule that people should never have admin access unless strictly necessary
summary: A core cybersecurity principle dictating that users, accounts, and processes are granted only the minimum permissions necessary to perform their assigned functions.

label: Linter
plain_descriptions: a tool that scans your code to find style errors, suspicious patterns, and potential bugs
an automated spell-checker for programming languages
summary: A static code analysis tool that inspects source code for programmatic errors, stylistic inconsistencies, security antipatterns, and non-standard syntax before runtime.

label: Large Language Model
plain_descriptions: an AI that writes text by guessing the next word
the kind of chatbot brain behind ChatGPT, Gemini or Claude
summary: A very large neural network trained on huge amounts of text that reads and writes language by predicting the next token.

label: Eval
plain_descriptions: an automated or human test process used to score an AI model's answers
measuring how well a language model performs on real-world business tasks
summary: A systematic evaluation methodology using automated judges, deterministic checks, or human grading to measure language model quality, safety, and correctness.

label: Load balancer
plain_descriptions: a traffic cop that distributes incoming website visitors evenly across multiple backend servers
a device or service preventing any single server from becoming overwhelmed by web requests
summary: A networking component that distributes incoming application or network traffic across a pool of backend destination servers.

label: Log
plain_descriptions: a timestamped text record written by software to explain what it just did
the running diary of events, errors, and actions that an application keeps
summary: A timestamped, discrete record of an event or state change emitted by a running computer program or system service.

label: Low-Rank Adaptation
plain_descriptions: a cheap way to fine-tune by training only a small add-on
small adapter files that teach a big model a new skill
summary: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that freezes the original weights and trains small low-rank matrices that represent the weight update.

label: Loss function
plain_descriptions: the mathematical scoring system that measures how wrong an AI model's answers are
a formula calculating the penalty when predictions deviate from true outcomes
summary: A mathematical function quantifying the discrepancy between a model's predicted outputs and true ground-truth targets.

label: Machine learning
plain_descriptions: software that learns rules from examples instead of explicit programming
computer systems improving their accuracy automatically through experience
summary: A branch of artificial intelligence where computer systems detect underlying patterns in data to improve task performance without static rule engines.

label: Margin
plain_descriptions: using assets in a brokerage account as collateral to borrow money for securities
the equity required in an account when buying securities with borrowed money
summary: Assets in a brokerage account support a loan used to buy securities.

label: Model Context Protocol
plain_descriptions: a standard plug that lets AI apps connect to tools and data
one common way for chatbots to talk to other software
summary: An open protocol that standardises how AI applications connect to external tools, data sources and workflows through MCP servers.

label: Merge conflict
plain_descriptions: a dispute where two branches edited the same lines of a file and Git cannot choose automatically
a clash in version control that requires manual human intervention to reconcile differing changes
summary: A state in version control that arises when competing changes are made to the same lines of code or when one branch modifies a file that another branch deletes, preventing automatic merging.

label: Message queue
plain_descriptions: a digital waiting line where servers leave jobs for worker programs to process one by one
a buffer holding background tasks so web servers stay responsive during heavy traffic
summary: An asynchronous communication component that stores messages in sequence until receiving consumer services retrieve and process them.

label: Metric
plain_descriptions: a numerical measurement tracked over time to see how busy or healthy a computer system is
aggregated statistics like CPU percentage, memory usage, or requests per second
summary: A quantifiable, aggregated numerical measurement recorded at regular time intervals to evaluate system performance and health.

label: Multi-factor authentication (MFA)
plain_descriptions: logging in with two different proofs such as your password plus a code sent to your phone
a security checkpoint requiring a password and a fingerprint before opening an account
summary: An authentication security method requiring users to supply two or more distinct evidence factors before granting access to a digital system.

label: Microservices
plain_descriptions: building software as a suite of small, independent services that communicate over a network
an architectural style where each business capability runs in its own deployable process
summary: An architectural style that structures an application as a collection of small, independently deployable, and loosely coupled services communicating via lightweight protocols.

label: Model
plain_descriptions: the trained software artifact that makes AI predictions
an algorithm packed with learned weights ready to run
summary: A mathematical representation trained on data that captures patterns to generate predictions, decisions, or new content.

label: Mock
plain_descriptions: a simulated software stand-in used to test code without calling real external services
a fake object that checks whether expected functions were called with correct parameters
summary: A simulated object that mimics the behavior of a real component in controlled ways, allowing developers to verify interactions and method invocations in isolation.

label: Parameter
plain_descriptions: the internal numerical values that an AI adjusts as it learns
the weights and biases inside a model that define how it responds
summary: An internal numerical variable within a model, such as a weight or bias, whose value is learned and updated directly from training data.

label: Training
plain_descriptions: the computational process of teaching an AI model using data
feeding examples into an algorithm so it can adjust its internal weights
summary: The iterative computational process of calculating errors and adjusting model weights against training data to minimize loss.

label: Monorepo
plain_descriptions: storing multiple distinct projects, apps, and shared libraries inside one single repository
a unified code repository holding all the different services of an organization
summary: A software development approach and repository architecture where multiple separate projects, applications, and shared libraries reside within a single version control repository.

label: MoSCoW method
plain_descriptions: prioritization technique that sorts requirements into Must have, Should have, Could have, and Won't have
categorization method ensuring teams deliver essential deliverables first while managing scope expectations
summary: A qualitative prioritization technique sorting project requirements into four distinct categories: Must have, Should have, Could have, and Won't have.

label: Minimum Viable Product (MVP)
plain_descriptions: simplest early version of a product built with just enough features to test with real users
functional initial release designed to validate core business hypotheses with minimal engineering effort
summary: An early iteration of a product incorporating the minimum feature set necessary to validate foundational assumptions with real customers.

label: Neural network
plain_descriptions: an AI computing structure inspired by interconnected biological brain cells
layered mathematical nodes passing signals forward to identify complex patterns
summary: A computational architecture comprising interconnected layers of artificial nodes that pass weighted signals through non-linear activation functions.

label: North Star metric
plain_descriptions: single key metric that best captures the core value a product delivers to its customers
overarching guiding metric that aligns product, engineering, and marketing teams toward long-term growth
summary: The primary operational metric capturing the core value delivered to customers that serves as the leading indicator of sustainable business growth.

label: OAuth
plain_descriptions: the security system that lets you log in with Google without giving your password to third-party apps
a delegation protocol granting limited permissions to an app on your behalf
summary: An open standard authorization framework that enables third-party applications to obtain limited access to protected user resources without sharing user passwords.

label: Object detection
plain_descriptions: an AI vision task that identifies multiple items in a photo and draws bounding boxes around them
finding where objects are located in an image and labeling each one
summary: A computer vision technique that simultaneously identifies the semantic class and spatial coordinates of multiple individual objects within an image.

label: Observability
plain_descriptions: understanding what is happening inside a complex system just by looking at its outputs and data
the ability to diagnose unknown software problems using telemetry data
summary: The extent to which the internal states and execution paths of complex software systems can be inferred solely from their external telemetry outputs.

label: Objectives and Key Results (OKR)
plain_descriptions: goal-setting system that pairs an inspiring objective with measurable numerical results
quarterly framework aligning company direction, team focus, and quantifiable targets
summary: A collaborative goal-setting framework pairing ambitious qualitative objectives with measurable key results to track organizational progress.

label: On-call
plain_descriptions: being available outside normal hours to respond immediately if production software breaks
the scheduled shift where an engineer carries the alert pager and fixes critical outages
summary: An operational duty rotation where designated engineers remain available to receive alerts and remediate critical production incidents outside or during standard working hours.

label: Object-Relational Mapping (ORM)
plain_descriptions: a programming bridge that lets developers query database tables using normal code objects
software that translates programming objects into SQL database rows automatically
summary: A software technique that bridges object-oriented code and relational databases by mapping database tables to programming language classes.

label: Overfitting
plain_descriptions: when an AI memorizes practice data so closely that it fails on fresh inputs
an AI model scoring near perfect in practice tests but failing real exams
summary: A modeling pathology where an algorithm learns idiosyncratic noise in training samples, severely impairing its ability to generalize to unseen data.

label: Pagination
plain_descriptions: dividing huge lists of data into smaller chunks across multiple pages
loading search results ten or twenty items at a time instead of everything at once
summary: A design technique that breaks large data sets into discrete subsets or pages to manage bandwidth and system performance.

label: Postmortem
plain_descriptions: a written report created after a major outage to understand what happened and prevent it from recurring
a blameless analysis of a system failure explaining the timeline, causes, and action items
summary: A structured, blameless written analysis document reviewing a production incident to identify root causes and assign preventative action items.

label: Product Requirements Document (PRD)
plain_descriptions: comprehensive guide detailing what problem a feature solves, what it should do, and how success is measured
foundational specification shared between product managers, designers, and software engineers
summary: A definitive planning document detailing product purpose, target personas, functional requirements, and measurable success criteria for delivery teams.

label: Principal
plain_descriptions: original sum of money borrowed or invested
money before any interest gets calculated
summary: The original sum of money lent, invested, or borrowed before interest accrues.

label: Product backlog
plain_descriptions: prioritized master list of features, bug fixes, and technical tasks waiting to be built
single authoritative repository of planned work for the entire software product team
summary: An evolving, ordered catalog of features, enhancements, and fixes representing the single source of work for a product team.

label: Product discovery
plain_descriptions: research and experimentation process used to figure out what product is worth building before writing code
systematic validation of customer problems, usability, feasibility, and business viability
summary: The exploratory process of validating customer problems and potential product solutions to ensure engineering teams build valuable, viable offerings.

label: Product-market fit
plain_descriptions: stage where a product satisfies strong customer demand in a large and viable market
state where customers love a product, retention stabilizes, and growth happens organically
summary: The commercial milestone achieved when a product satisfies the demands of an attractive market, evidenced by sustained user retention and organic adoption.

label: Product owner (PO)
plain_descriptions: person responsible for deciding what features a product should have and setting their priority
key team member who connects user needs and business goals with development work
summary: The Scrum role accountable for maximizing product value and managing the prioritized content of the product backlog.

label: Release
plain_descriptions: formal deployment and launch of a finished software version to end users
milestone package combining tested features, bug fixes, and documentation into production
summary: The formal deployment and distribution of a production-ready software version to customers alongside associated release notes and assets.

label: Product roadmap
plain_descriptions: high-level strategic timeline communicating where a product is heading and why
visual guide that aligns executives, developers, and customers on major product milestones
summary: A strategic, evolving visual document mapping the vision, overarching direction, and planned milestones of a product over time.

label: Profit margin
plain_descriptions: how much profit a company keeps from each dollar of revenue
the percentage of sales that remains as profit
summary: A percentage comparing a specified measure of profit with the corresponding revenue.

label: Prompt
plain_descriptions: what you type to tell the AI what to do
the question or instructions you give a chatbot
summary: The text, and sometimes images or files, given to a language model as input to steer what it produces.

label: Prompt caching
plain_descriptions: saving the unchanging start of a prompt so later calls are cheaper and faster
not paying full price to resend the same long instructions
summary: A provider feature that keeps the processed beginning of a prompt so later requests starting the same way cost less and answer faster.

label: Prompt injection
plain_descriptions: tricking an AI with hidden instructions in text it reads
a web page or file that secretly tells the chatbot to misbehave
summary: An attack in which crafted input, typed by a user or hidden in content the model reads, overrides the application’s intended instructions.

label: Pull request (PR)
plain_descriptions: a formal request asking teammates to review and merge your branch into the main codebase
a shared discussion page displaying proposed code changes in version control
summary: A mechanism in distributed version control platforms that allows a developer to propose changes from a feature branch and request peer review before merging.

label: Quantization
plain_descriptions: compressing an AI model by using fewer bits to store each number
reducing model precision from 16-bit floats to 8-bit or 4-bit integers to save memory
summary: A model compression technique that maps high-precision numerical weights to lower-bit representations to reduce memory footprint and boost inference speed.

label: Race condition
plain_descriptions: a bug where program behavior changes unpredictably depending on which task finishes first
a timing flaw occurring when multiple threads try to modify the same shared data at once
summary: An undesirable condition in concurrent programming where system behavior or output depends unpredictably on the relative execution order or timing of uncontrollable events.

label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
plain_descriptions: letting the AI look things up in your documents before it answers
a chatbot that answers from a company’s own files
summary: A technique that retrieves relevant documents when a question arrives and adds them to the prompt so the model answers from them.

label: Rate limiting
plain_descriptions: restricting how many times a user or app can call an API within a minute or hour to stop abuse
a traffic cap preventing servers from crashing when too many requests arrive at once
summary: A defensive network control mechanism that caps the number of requests a client can submit to an API or service within a specified time window.

label: Reasoning model
plain_descriptions: an AI model that spends extra computational time thinking step-by-step before answering
an advanced language model trained to reason through complex math and logic puzzles internally
summary: A language model trained to produce intermediate reasoning tokens, often hidden or summarized for the user, to deliberate and verify multi-step plans before emitting final answers.

label: Refactoring
plain_descriptions: cleaning up internal code without changing what the program actually does
reorganizing software logic to make it cleaner and easier to maintain
summary: The disciplined technique of restructuring existing source code to improve readability and maintainability without altering observable external behavior.

label: Regression testing
plain_descriptions: re-running existing tests to make sure new code changes haven't broken old features
verifying that fixing one software bug didn't accidentally introduce new problems
summary: The practice of re-executing test suites against an updated application to ensure that recent code modifications or bug fixes have not disrupted previously working functionality.

label: REST
plain_descriptions: standard rules for how websites and apps exchange data over the web
the way modern apps talk to servers using standard web addresses
summary: An architectural style for network applications that uses standard HTTP methods to manipulate resources identified by URIs.

label: Retention rate
plain_descriptions: percentage of users who continue using or paying for an app over a given timeframe
metric demonstrating how effectively a product keeps existing customers engaged over time
summary: The percentage of customers that a business retains over a specified duration, reflecting enduring product value and satisfaction.

label: RICE scoring
plain_descriptions: formula to rank features by multiplying reach, impact, and confidence, then dividing by effort
scoring model helping product managers objectively decide which projects deliver the highest return on investment
summary: A quantitative prioritization framework that scores potential initiatives by multiplying Reach, Impact, and Confidence and dividing by Effort.

label: Return on Investment
plain_descriptions: how much money you make back compared to what you spent
performance metric measuring profitability of an expense
summary: A performance metric used to evaluate the efficiency or profitability of an investment relative to its cost.

label: Rollback
plain_descriptions: quickly switching back to the previous working version of software when a new release has critical bugs
reverting a deployment to restore system stability after an update causes failures
summary: The operational action of reverting an application, configuration, or database deployment to a previously verified stable release.

label: Scope creep
plain_descriptions: uncontrolled growth in project features and requirements without adding extra time or budget
gradual piling on of unplanned requests that derails software delivery schedules
summary: The gradual and uncontrolled expansion of project scope beyond initial goals without corresponding adjustments to schedule, budget, or resources.

label: Scrum
plain_descriptions: collaborative framework for developing complex products in short timeboxed iterations
structured agile method featuring specific roles, backlogs, and iterative review meetings
summary: A lightweight process framework structured around transparency, inspection, and adaptation to build products incrementally.

label: Scrum master
plain_descriptions: coach who guides the team in agile practices and removes blockers that slow down development
facilitator who protects engineers from external distractions and improves team collaboration
summary: The Scrum role accountable for establishing Scrum practices, promoting team effectiveness, and removing operational impediments.

label: Software Development Kit (SDK)
plain_descriptions: an all-in-one toolbox for building software for a specific platform
a prepackaged set of tools and code libraries provided to developers
summary: A comprehensive collection of development tools, client libraries, documentation, and code samples designed for creating applications on a specific platform or service.

label: Secret
plain_descriptions: sensitive data like passwords, API keys, and encryption certificates that must never be saved in public code
secure configuration credentials that grant software access to databases and external services
summary: A sensitive configuration asset, such as an authentication token, password, private key, or certificate, requiring strict encryption and access control.

label: Semantic versioning
plain_descriptions: a three-part version numbering system showing whether updates contain fixes, new features, or breaking changes
a standard release labeling scheme formatted as MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH to signal compatibility
summary: A formal versioning specification utilizing a three-part numbering format (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) to communicate the compatibility nature of software changes.

label: Serverless
plain_descriptions: running code in the cloud without renting, managing, or patching any physical or virtual servers
a cloud pricing and compute model where you only pay for the exact milliseconds your code executes
summary: A cloud computing execution model where the cloud provider dynamically manages server infrastructure and charges only for resource consumption during code execution.

label: Sharding
plain_descriptions: splitting a massive database table across multiple separate computers so it can handle huge traffic
dividing customer records across server A, B, and C based on user ID regions
summary: A database architecture pattern that horizontally partitions a single logical dataset across multiple independent physical database instances.

label: Side effect
plain_descriptions: any change a function makes outside of simply returning a value
modifying global variables, writing files, or updating databases as a result of executing code
summary: Any observable change in program state or interaction with the outside world produced by a function or expression beyond returning its computed value.

label: Simple Interest
plain_descriptions: interest calculated solely on the initial deposit
fixed interest payment that never compounds
summary: Interest calculated exclusively on the original principal amount for the entirety of the loan or deposit period.

label: Service Level Agreement (SLA)
plain_descriptions: a formal contract between a service provider and a customer promising a level of uptime with financial penalties if missed
the business agreement that specifies compensation if a service suffers excessive outages
summary: A formal commitment between a service provider and clients specifying agreed service performance thresholds and contractual penalties for non-compliance.

label: Service Level Indicator (SLI)
plain_descriptions: the exact number measuring how well a service is actually performing right now
the measured metric used to check if an engineering team is meeting its reliability targets
summary: A carefully chosen quantitative metric that measures the actual level of service delivered to users over time.

label: Service Level Objective (SLO)
plain_descriptions: an internal reliability goal that engineering teams aim to achieve for their service
the agreed target percentage of uptime or speed that keeps users satisfied
summary: A precise, target reliability threshold specified by engineering teams to determine acceptable service quality over an extended duration.

label: Container
plain_descriptions: a lightweight sandbox containing an app and its dependencies to run anywhere reliably
an isolated environment running software using shared operating system resources
summary: A standard unit of software packaging code and all runtime dependencies to execute reliably in isolation on a shared OS kernel.

label: Dependency
plain_descriptions: an external package or library that your application relies on to function
a third-party software component required to run or compile your project
summary: An external library, module, package, or service that a software program requires in order to compile, execute, or deliver its intended functionality.

label: Deployment
plain_descriptions: the process of installing and activating a new version of software on live servers
rolling out updated application packages to make them accessible to users
summary: The operational process of releasing, installing, configuring, and activating a software version in a target hosting environment.

label: Framework
plain_descriptions: a foundational software skeleton that dictates how your application is built and executed
a platform that calls your custom code within a predefined structural architecture
summary: A comprehensive structural foundation providing generic functionality, application lifecycle control, and architectural conventions into which custom code is inserted.

label: Library
plain_descriptions: a collection of reusable code routines that your program calls when needed
a package of pre-written functions you import to perform specific tasks
summary: A packaged collection of pre-written functions, classes, and subroutines that developers import and call directly to accomplish specific programmatic tasks.

label: Sprint
plain_descriptions: fixed development timebox usually running two weeks to build working features
regular repeating cycle where a team converts selected backlog tasks into finished software
summary: A timeboxed iteration of one month or less during which a team builds a functional, verified product increment.

label: Sprint planning
plain_descriptions: collaborative meeting held at the start of a sprint to decide what work to tackle next
planning session where the team establishes a sprint goal and selects backlog items
summary: The collaborative event initiating each sprint where the Scrum team defines the sprint goal and forecasts backlog delivery.

label: Sprint retrospective
plain_descriptions: end-of-sprint team meeting to review what went well and identify concrete ways to improve
safe reflective space where teammates evaluate tools, processes, and interpersonal collaboration
summary: The final event of a sprint where the Scrum team inspects its past performance regarding people, relationships, process, and tools to identify actionable improvements.

label: SQL
plain_descriptions: the standard computer language used to ask questions and edit data in relational databases
the command language for reading, filtering, and inserting rows in tables like postgres or mysql
summary: A standardized declarative programming language used to manage, query, and manipulate data stored in relational database management systems.

label: SQL injection
plain_descriptions: a security hack where attackers trick a website into running rogue database commands
typing malicious sql codes into login forms to steal data or bypass passwords
summary: A web security vulnerability that allows an attacker to interfere with backend database queries by injecting malicious SQL statements into input fields.

label: Staging environment
plain_descriptions: a private test replica of the live website used for final quality checks before public release
the pre-production sandbox where software is tested under near-identical production conditions
summary: A pre-production testing environment that mirrors the exact hardware, architecture, and configuration of the production system to conduct final verification.

label: Stakeholder
plain_descriptions: anyone who has an interest in, influences, or is affected by the outcome of a product
key parties connected to a project, including end users, business leaders, investors, and regulatory bodies
summary: An individual, team, or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive itself to be affected by a product decision or outcome.

label: Story point
plain_descriptions: abstract measurement unit used to estimate the relative effort, complexity, and risk of a software task
scoring system that rates user story difficulty using relative comparisons rather than calendar hours
summary: A relative number that agile teams use to estimate how much total effort a backlog item will take, compared with other items.

label: Structured output
plain_descriptions: making the AI reply in an exact data format
getting JSON back instead of free text
summary: Model output constrained to follow a given format, usually a JSON schema, so that software can read it reliably.

label: Subagent
plain_descriptions: a specialized helper AI spawned by a main agent to handle a specific subtask
a secondary AI assistant focused on one piece of a larger project
summary: A specialized agent spawned and coordinated by a primary supervisor agent to execute an isolated, narrow task within a multi-agent system.

label: System prompt
plain_descriptions: hidden instructions an app gives the AI before you start chatting
the rules that set an assistant’s role and tone
summary: Instructions placed before the conversation that set the model’s role, rules and style for every later message.

label: Technical debt
plain_descriptions: the future cost of choosing a quick and dirty coding shortcut today
implied rework created when speedy software delivery sacrifices clean architecture
summary: The accumulated implied cost of additional future rework caused by choosing an expedited, suboptimal technical solution instead of a well-architected approach.

label: Temperature
plain_descriptions: an AI setting that controls how creative or predictable generated text will be
a dial adjusting randomness in model answers from strictly factual to imaginative
summary: A sampling hyperparameter that scales logits before softmax to regulate the randomness and diversity of a language model's output tokens.

label: Throughput
plain_descriptions: the total amount of work or data a computer system can process in one second
the volume of web requests or megabytes moving through a service over time
summary: The rate at which a computer system, communication channel, or application successfully processes and delivers data or transactions per unit of time.

label: Transport Layer Security (TLS)
plain_descriptions: the security protocol that powers the padlock icon and https in your browser address bar
an encrypted communications tunnel protecting internet traffic from eavesdropping and tampering
summary: A cryptographic communication protocol that provides privacy, data integrity, and authentication for communications over computer networks.

label: Token
plain_descriptions: digital access pass sent with web requests
encoded string proving you are logged in
summary: A cryptographically signed string presented to servers to prove identity and authorization permissions.

label: Token
plain_descriptions: digital asset issued on an existing blockchain
utility or governance coin within a decentralized app
summary: A digital unit of value issued on top of an existing smart contract blockchain platform.

label: Token
plain_descriptions: unit AI uses to count text chunks
why AI charges per prompt length
summary: Small chunk of text, typically subword units, processed by large language models.

label: Tokenizer
plain_descriptions: the part that chops text into pieces the AI can read
what decides how many tokens a sentence costs
summary: The component that splits input such as text into tokens from a fixed vocabulary and turns them into numeric ids for the model.

label: Top-p sampling
plain_descriptions: picking next AI words only from the most probable group that adds up to p
an AI text sampling rule that cuts off unlikely, bizarre words dynamically
summary: A text generation decoding strategy that selects from the smallest subset of candidate tokens whose cumulative probability reaches a threshold p.

label: Transformer
plain_descriptions: the neural network design that powers modern large language models
an architecture that connects words across entire passages at once using self-attention
summary: A neural network architecture relying on self-attention mechanisms to process sequence elements in parallel without recurrent connections.

label: Type checking
plain_descriptions: verifying that variables and function arguments hold the expected kinds of data
catching mismatched data types before or during program execution
summary: The verification process that evaluates whether data values assigned to variables or passed to functions comply with the rules of a programming language type system.

label: Unit test
plain_descriptions: an automated check testing the smallest single piece of code in isolation
verifying that an individual function returns the correct answer for given inputs
summary: An automated test that isolates and verifies the behavioral correctness of the smallest testable component or function of an application.

label: Uptime
plain_descriptions: the percentage of time a computer system or website is running and ready for users
how long a service stays available without crashing or going offline
summary: The proportion or duration of time that a computer system, network, or application remains fully functional and accessible to users.

label: User story
plain_descriptions: short informal description of a software feature framed from the perspective of an end user
practical work item explaining who needs a capability, what they need, and why it provides value
summary: A concise, non-technical explanation of a software requirement capturing user intent, desired functionality, and business value.

label: Vector database
plain_descriptions: a database that finds things by similar meaning
storage that searches by how close lists of numbers are
summary: A database built to store embedding vectors and quickly return the ones most similar to a query vector.

label: Velocity
plain_descriptions: average amount of work a development team delivers during a single sprint
historical metric measuring how many story points a squad completes per iteration
summary: A planning metric tracking the average volume of story points or backlog items completed by a team per sprint.

label: Virtual machine (VM)
plain_descriptions: a software simulation of an entire physical computer running its own complete operating system
a virtual computer created inside a powerful server that behaves just like a physical machine
summary: A software emulation of a physical computer system that executes applications within a dedicated, isolated guest operating system managed by a hypervisor.

label: Session
plain_descriptions: the server-side record remembering who you are while you click around a website
the active conversation state linking multiple web page clicks to one logged-in user
summary: A server-side state mechanism that tracks an individual user’s interactions and identity across multiple stateless HTTP requests.

label: Webhook
plain_descriptions: an automatic notification sent between servers as soon as something happens
a reverse phone call where a payment provider rings your app to say money arrived
summary: An automated HTTP POST callback triggered by an origin system to deliver real-time event payloads to external receiver endpoints.

label: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
plain_descriptions: a vulnerability where attackers inject malicious javascript into a website to hijack visitor browsers
sneaking rogue code into public comment sections so readers' login cookies get stolen
summary: A web application flaw permitting attackers to embed rogue executable scripts into viewed pages, running unauthorized actions inside visitor browsers.

label: Zero trust
plain_descriptions: a security model that never assumes any user or device is safe, even inside the office network
the principle of verifying identity and device health for every single digital request
summary: A cybersecurity framework requiring continuous verification of every user, device, and network transaction, operating under the assumption that breaches are already present.
